title: [CQ-R11e1] Host pinned Node toolchain cache
description:
Objective: the host obtains the exact pinned official Node.js Linux release tarball, for x64 and arm64, to serve as the check VM's toolchain. It is verified by sha256 and cached controller-private, and the network is never trusted for its identity. This is the toolchain half of the human's CQ-R11e decision, made in the architect REPL on 2026-10-30: an OFFLINE CACHE, so the check guest never touches the network.

Split from CQ-R11e (task-001d8ab3) by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-30. It depends on CQ-R10d2 (task-4017cf1d), whose downloader it shares.

Deliverable:
- A new scripts/local-runner/toolchain.json: {schemaVersion:1, node:{x64:{version, url, sha256, size}, arm64:{...}}}.
  - Each url must equal the fixed template https://nodejs.org/dist/v<version>/node-v<version>-linux-<x64|arm64>.tar.xz. A .tar.gz is acceptable instead; pick ONE form and pin it.
  - The worker picks the current Active LTS, downloads each file once, cross-checks nodejs.org's SHASUMS256.txt, and records the version, hashes and sizes in the step note.
- Refactor scripts/local-runner/agent-cache.mjs (CQ-R10d2) to EXPORT its bounded https download-and-verify core: manual https-only redirects, a size bound, an exclusive .part, an atomic rename, and re-verification on a cache hit. fetchAgentBinary's behavior and every R10d2 test stay unchanged.
- A new scripts/local-runner/toolchain-cache.mjs with loadToolchainManifest() and fetchNodeToolchain({arch, cacheDir}, {fetch, manifest}), which resolves a frozen {file, sha256, size, version}. The tarball stays WHOLE; CQ-R11e2 extracts it in the guest.
- Tests use an injected fetch, never the network. They live in scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs, and scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs's `required` list gains toolchain.json and toolchain-cache.mjs.

Scope boundaries:
- No guest install (CQ-R11e2), no dependency cache (CQ-R11e3), no orchestration or environment identity (CQ-R11e).
- No .moe edits; no verified-local or isolation claim.
- Fixed error codes, with no URL, path or body in any message.
- If the official files cannot be downloaded from this environment, report_blocked; never invent a hash.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH)
definitionOfDone: The toolchain manifest loader accepts only the exact pinned shape, with the fixed nodejs.org https URL template, and refuses anything else with a fixed code. Shown by tests.

fetchNodeToolchain keeps a tarball only when its bytes match the pinned sha256 and size. A mismatch, an oversized body, a non-https redirect or an interrupted transfer fails closed with no file left, and a cache hit is re-verified. Shown by tests with an injected fetch.
fetchAgentBinary's behavior and every CQ-R10d2 test are unchanged by the shared-downloader refactor.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development. Plan against LANDED bytes, so re-read them first:
- R10d2's scripts/local-runner/agent-cache.mjs: fetchAgentBinary, holdsPin, cached, respond, writeBody, writePart and download;
- R10d2's AB-row harness in scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs: routes, redirected, refused and the AB3 cpSync module copy;
- R11e3a's DA section at the end of scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs.

scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs: add a section '// CQ-R11e1: the host's pinned Node toolchain cache (rows TC1-TC7)' at the end. Keep the helper names and shapes stable; CQ-R11e3's approved plan reuses them, along with sha() and caught().

Helpers:
- fixtureFetch(table): an injected fetch over fixture routes, shaped like R10d2's routes(). Each url maps to [status, body chunks (an Error chunk fails the stream) or a thrown Error, headers, final url]. Each call records [url, init.redirect, init.signal instanceof AbortSignal]. It returns {fetch, calls}.
- redirected(url, count, chunks): as R10d2's.
- toolchainAt(arch, bytes): the SHIPPED toolchain.json with that arch's sha256 and size swapped for the fixture's; its url stays the real template.
- refusedAs(code, messages): asserts that [error.code, error.message, Object.keys(error)] deep-equals [code, messages[code], ['code']].
- TOOLCHAIN_MESSAGES and PINNED_MESSAGES: the fixed texts from steps 3 and 4.
- A scratch-dir helper with after() cleanup.

Rows, table-driven:
- TC1 (DoD 1). loadToolchainManifest() deep-equals the shipped JSON and is deep-frozen. For x64 and arm64, url === `https://nodejs.org/dist/v${version}/node-v${version}-linux-${arch}.tar.xz`, and both arches share one version. That version's major equals every `node-version: '<n>'` in .github/workflows/ci.yml. This is the human's 2026-10-30 decision: the check VM runs CI's Node line.
- TC2 (DoD 1). validateToolchainManifest refuses each of these with TOOLCHAIN_MANIFEST_INVALID:
  - not an object; schemaVersion 2; an extra top-level key; no node; an extra tool beside node; a missing or extra arch; a missing or extra entry key;
  - an http url; a url with another host, another version, .tar.gz, a query string or a trailing slash;
  - version 'v24.22.2', '24.22', '24.22.2-rc.1' or '024.1.0';
  - x64 and arm64 on different versions;
  - an uppercase or 63-char sha256;
  - size 0, -1, 1.5, '1' or 134217729.
  fetchNodeToolchain with each of them as its manifest seam refuses the same way, before any fetch call.
  The 64 KiB bound: cpSync the local-runner dir into scratch and import the copy's toolchain-cache.mjs by file URL, as AB3 does. A toolchain.json of exactly 65_536 bytes loads. 65_537 bytes, not-JSON and a missing file are each TOOLCHAIN_MANIFEST_INVALID.
- TC3 (DoD 2). A body matching its pins, after 0 and after 5 https redirects (the later Locations relative), is kept at <cacheDir>/<sha256>.tar.xz.
  - The result deep-equals the frozen {file, sha256, size, version}, with keys in that order.
  - cacheDir holds only that file, with the body's bytes. On POSIX, cacheDir is 0700 and the file 0600.
  - Every call was [url, 'manual', true].
- TC4 (DoD 2). Each case fails closed and leaves readdirSync(cacheDir) === []:
  - another sha256, or a short body: TOOLCHAIN_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH;
  - a declared content-length over the pin, or a streamed body over it: TOOLCHAIN_TOO_LARGE;
  - a redirect to http, a chain of 6, a redirect without Location, a 404, a thrown fetch, a body that errors midway, or a response whose url is http: TOOLCHAIN_DOWNLOAD_FAILED.
  Every refusal passes refusedAs(code, TOOLCHAIN_MESSAGES): no URL, path or body.
- TC5 (DoD 2). A valid cached file resolves with zero fetch calls. One flipped byte: the file is removed, fetched exactly once more, and verified. A directory at the target, or (POSIX only) a symlink to a valid file, is TOOLCHAIN_INPUT_INVALID with zero fetches, and is never followed or deleted. Two concurrent calls both resolve the same result and leave no .part.
- TC6 (the export, for CQ-R11e3). fetchPinnedFile with algorithm 'sha512', size null and maxBytes:
  - a matching body is kept at file and resolves the frozen {file, size};
  - a body over maxBytes is PINNED_TOO_LARGE, and another digest is PINNED_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH. Neither leaves a file;
  - each of these is PINNED_INPUT_INVALID before any fetch: an http url; a relative file; a file with a control character; algorithm 'md5'; a digest of the wrong length, or uppercase; size over maxBytes; maxBytes 0 or over MAX_AGENT_BINARY_BYTES; a fetch that is not a function.
  Refusals pass refusedAs(code, PINNED_MESSAGES).
- TC7. fetchNodeToolchain refuses with TOOLCHAIN_INPUT_INVALID, before any fetch or mkdir: a missing or non-record input; arch 'ia32'; a relative cacheDir; a cacheDir with a control character; a fetch that is not a function.

implementationPlan.description:
Pin the Node.js toolchain in the new scripts/local-runner/toolchain.json.

Human decision, architect REPL, 2026-10-30: pin CI's Node line, NOT the newest Active LTS.
- Every node-version in ci.yml and release.yml is '24'. Node 26 became Active LTS on 2026-10-28, but the check VM must run the same major as CI.
- The version is the newest 24.x in https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json at the time you pin; on 2026-10-30 that was v24.22.2.
- Use .tar.xz for both arches, the smaller file. CQ-R11e2's guest extracts it with tarfile 'r:*' and lzma, which Ubuntu 24.04's python3 ships.

Shape, compact and hand-reviewable like agent-binaries.json:
{"schemaVersion": 1, "node": {"x64": {"version", "url", "sha256", "size"}, "arm64": {...}}}
url is exactly https://nodejs.org/dist/v<version>/node-v<version>-linux-<arch>.tar.xz.

Download each file ONCE over https, into a scratch dir outside the repo.
- Compute the sha256 and the byte size from the downloaded bytes.
- Cross-check both against https://nodejs.org/dist/v<version>/SHASUMS256.txt.
- For reference, the architect's HEAD requests on 2026-10-30 saw 32039312 bytes for x64 and 30968168 for arm64, with no redirect.
- Record the version, both hashes and sizes, and the cross-check in this step's note.
- Delete the scratch downloads afterwards. The repo carries only the manifest.

This step's error handling: if nodejs.org cannot be reached, or a hash disagrees with SHASUMS256.txt, stop and call moe.report_blocked. Never invent or guess a hash, and never copy one from anywhere but the downloaded bytes.

implementationPlan.description:
Refactor scripts/local-runner/agent-cache.mjs, starting from R10d2's LANDED bytes, so that its download-and-verify core is ONE exported function. DoD 3: fetchAgentBinary's behavior, codes, messages and on-disk results stay unchanged, and so does every AB1-AB11 row.

1. Neutral codes for the core. PINNED_MESSAGES:
   - PINNED_INPUT_INVALID 'The pinned download request was invalid.'
   - PINNED_DOWNLOAD_FAILED 'The pinned file could not be downloaded.'
   - PINNED_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH 'The pinned file did not match its checksum.'
   - PINNED_TOO_LARGE 'The pinned file exceeded its size bound.'
   - PINNED_UNREADABLE 'The cached pinned file could not be read.'
   The shared internals (holdsPin, cached, respond, writeBody, writePart and the download stage) throw these instead of AGENT_BINARY_ codes. parseHeader and untar keep AGENT_BINARY_ARCHIVE_INVALID and AGENT_BINARY_TOO_LARGE, because the archive path belongs to the agent alone.
2. fetchAgentBinary's refuse() maps PINNED_<kind> to AGENT_BINARY_<kind> one to one, before its MESSAGES lookup and its DOWNLOAD_FAILED fallback. Every error that leaves fetchAgentBinary goes through it, cached() included, so callers see exactly the codes and texts that AB1-AB11 pin.
3. Generalize the pin the internals take to {url, size, maxBytes, algorithm, digest}:
   - algorithm is 'sha256' or 'sha512', and digest is lowercase hex of that algorithm's length;
   - size is the exact byte count, or null when only maxBytes bounds the body;
   - holdsPin hashes with createHash(algorithm), bounded by size ?? maxBytes, and returns the verified length or false;
   - the content-length check and writeBody use maxBytes.
4. Export one function, with a JSDoc documenting its options record (CQ-R11e3's plan reads it):
   `fetchPinnedFile({ url, file, size, maxBytes, algorithm, digest }, { fetch = globalThis.fetch } = {})`
   It resolves Object.freeze({ file, size }) once file holds verified bytes.
   - Validate first, before any fs or fetch call; anything invalid is PINNED_INPUT_INVALID:
     - url is a string whose URL protocol is https:;
     - file is an absolute path with no control character. Its directory already exists, because callers create it 0700;
     - size is null, or a positive safe integer of at most maxBytes;
     - maxBytes is a positive safe integer of at most MAX_AGENT_BINARY_BYTES;
     - algorithm and digest are as in item 3;
     - fetch is a function.
   - Then cached(file, pin), or else the download stage:
     - respond, with manual https-only redirects (at most 5) and the timeout;
     - an exclusive 0600 `.${digest}.${pid}.${random}.part` beside file, synced;
     - content-length and stream bounded by maxBytes;
     - holdsPin, then an atomic rename.
   - Every failure removes this call's .part and is a PINNED_ code with its fixed text. Anything unknown is PINNED_DOWNLOAD_FAILED.
   - It never creates directories, never extracts and never logs.
5. fetchAgentBinary:
   - A raw binary (claude) goes through fetchPinnedFile with {url: pin.url, file: target, size: pin.size, maxBytes: pin.size, algorithm: 'sha256', digest: pin.sha256}.
   - The archive path (codex) is exactly as landed: cached(target, member), then the same download stage for the archive .part, then untar, the member check and the rename.
   - The .part names stay `.${sha256}.${nonce}.part`.
6. Every existing export keeps its signature: AGENT_CLIS, MAX_AGENT_BINARY_BYTES, validateAgentManifest, loadAgentManifest and fetchAgentBinary. Add only fetchPinnedFile, and update the header comment.

Error handling: no PINNED_ code ever escapes fetchAgentBinary. No message carries a URL, a path or body bytes. The archive is still verified before untar, and the member before its rename.

Then `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs` must stay all green, with NO edit to that file, and TC6 turns green.
implementationPlan.note:
agent-cache.mjs refactored from R10d2's landed bytes (+80/-34). 
- PINNED_MESSAGES (5 fixed texts per plan); a shared fixed(messages, code, fallback); pinned() for the core; refuse() now maps PINNED_<kind> -> AGENT_BINARY_<kind> before its MESSAGES lookup/DOWNLOAD_FAILED fallback.
- holdsPin/cached/respond/writeBody/writePart/download throw PINNED_ codes. Pins are {url, size, maxBytes, algorithm, digest} (sha256Pin() adapts manifest entries); holdsPin hashes with createHash(algorithm), bounded by size ?? maxBytes, and returns the verified length or false; content-length and writeBody use maxBytes.
- download(pin, target, fetch, archive, member) keeps the landed shape: archive verified before untar, member verified before the atomic rename; .part names `.${digest}.${pid}.${rand}.part` beside target; its catch passes the archive path's own AGENT_BINARY_ codes through and turns anything else into a PINNED_ code.
- New export fetchPinnedFile({url, file, size, maxBytes, algorithm, digest}, {fetch}) with JSDoc of the options record: validates everything before any I/O (https string url, absolute control-free file, size null or 1..maxBytes, maxBytes 1..MAX_AGENT_BINARY_BYTES, algorithm sha256|sha512 via a Map (no key coercion), lowercase hex digest of that length, fetch a function), then cached() or download(), resolving Object.freeze({file, size}); its catch re-maps to fixed PINNED_ codes. Never mkdirs/extracts/logs.
- fetchAgentBinary: claude goes through fetchPinnedFile; codex is cached(target, member) then download with the archive; every error leaves through refuse(), so no PINNED_ code escapes. Existing exports and signatures unchanged.
Evidence: local-runner-agents.test.mjs NOT edited (git diff --quiet), env -i Node 24.21.0: 20/20 pass, AB1-AB11 green. TC6 runs once toolchain-cache.mjs exists (static imports), at step 4.

implementationPlan.description:
Create scripts/local-runner/toolchain-cache.mjs, the host cache of the pinned Node.js toolchain for the check VM.

Header comment, a few lines:
- the module-relative toolchain.json pins each arch's fixed nodejs.org https URL, sha256 and size;
- callers, the CLI and the environment cannot choose a manifest or a URL;
- integrity comes from the pins, through agent-cache.mjs fetchPinnedFile;
- the tarball stays whole, because CQ-R11e2 extracts it in the guest;
- cacheDir is controller-private and chosen by the caller;
- nothing here is an isolation claim.

Exports:
- MAX_TOOLCHAIN_BYTES = 134_217_728, the same bound CQ-R11e2's installToolchain enforces.
- validateToolchainManifest(value), checked on a structuredClone:
  - exact keys ['schemaVersion', 'node'], schemaVersion 1, and node keys exactly IMAGE_ARCHES;
  - each entry has exactly ['version', 'url', 'sha256', 'size'];
  - version follows the same strict x.y.z rule as agent-cache.mjs's VERSION; copy the regex, and do not widen agent-cache's exports;
  - url === `https://nodejs.org/dist/v${version}/node-v${version}-linux-${arch}.tar.xz`;
  - sha256 is 64 lowercase hex, and size is a positive safe integer of at most MAX_TOOLCHAIN_BYTES;
  - both arches carry the same version.
  It returns a deep-frozen copy. Anything else is TOOLCHAIN_MANIFEST_INVALID.
- loadToolchainManifest(): reads the module-relative toolchain.json, at most 65_536 bytes, then parses and validates it. Any failure is TOOLCHAIN_MANIFEST_INVALID.
- fetchNodeToolchain({ arch, cacheDir }, { fetch = globalThis.fetch, manifest } = {}):
  1. Validate the input before any fs or fetch call: a record, arch in IMAGE_ARCHES, an absolute cacheDir with no control character, and a function fetch. Anything else is TOOLCHAIN_INPUT_INVALID.
  2. manifest is a test seam only, validated by validateToolchainManifest like the installed one.
  3. mkdir(cacheDir, {recursive: true, mode: 0o700}). A failure is TOOLCHAIN_INPUT_INVALID.
  4. file = <cacheDir>/<sha256>.tar.xz. Call fetchPinnedFile({url, file, size, maxBytes: size, algorithm: 'sha256', digest: sha256}, {fetch}).
  5. A PINNED_<kind> rejection becomes TOOLCHAIN_<kind>, one to one, with this module's fixed text. Anything else is TOOLCHAIN_DOWNLOAD_FAILED.
  6. Resolve Object.freeze({ file, sha256, size, version }), in that key order.

Fixed texts, none carrying a URL, a path or body bytes:
- TOOLCHAIN_INPUT_INVALID 'The toolchain request was invalid.'
- TOOLCHAIN_MANIFEST_INVALID 'The installed toolchain manifest is invalid or unavailable.'
- TOOLCHAIN_DOWNLOAD_FAILED 'The pinned toolchain could not be downloaded.'
- TOOLCHAIN_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH 'The toolchain did not match its pinned checksum.'
- TOOLCHAIN_TOO_LARGE 'The toolchain exceeded its pinned size.'
- TOOLCHAIN_UNREADABLE 'The cached toolchain could not be read.'

Imports: only node:fs/promises, node:path, ./agent-cache.mjs (fetchPinnedFile) and ./guest-bootstrap.mjs (IMAGE_ARCHES). No new dependency.

Error handling: every rejection is a fixed TOOLCHAIN_ code, so CQ-R11e passes it through. A failed call leaves no file, because fetchPinnedFile cleans up its own .part.

Then TC1-TC7 and the bundle rows go green.
implementationPlan.note:
New scripts/local-runner/toolchain-cache.mjs (72 lines). Exports MAX_TOOLCHAIN_BYTES = 134_217_728, validateToolchainManifest (structuredClone copy; exact keys; schemaVersion 1; node keys exactly IMAGE_ARCHES; entry keys exactly version/url/sha256/size; strict x.y.z VERSION regex copied from agent-cache; url === the fixed nodejs.org .tar.xz template; lowercase sha256; size 1..MAX_TOOLCHAIN_BYTES; one version for both arches; deep-frozen), loadToolchainManifest (module-relative, <=65_536 bytes, any failure TOOLCHAIN_MANIFEST_INVALID) and fetchNodeToolchain({arch, cacheDir}, {fetch, manifest}) (input validated before any fs/fetch -> manifest -> mkdir 0700 -> fetchPinnedFile sha256 with maxBytes = size -> PINNED_<kind> mapped to TOOLCHAIN_<kind>, anything else TOOLCHAIN_DOWNLOAD_FAILED -> frozen {file, sha256, size, version}). Six fixed TOOLCHAIN_ texts, none with URL/path/body. Imports only node:fs/promises, node:path, ./agent-cache.mjs, ./guest-bootstrap.mjs.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the diff as a network attacker, and as a careless future caller of fetchPinnedFile.
- Is any byte trusted before its digest is checked? Is a cache hit re-verified on one no-follow descriptor?
- Can a caller's options reach a path outside the file's directory, follow a link or skip https? Is every option validated before any I/O?
- Is any .part left behind on any failure: an abort, a timeout, a stream error, a full disk or a failed rename?
- Does a PINNED code ever escape fetchAgentBinary or fetchNodeToolchain unmapped? Does any message carry a URL, a path or a body?
- Does the archive path still verify the archive before untar, and the member before the rename?
- Concurrency: unique .part names, an exclusive create, an atomic rename.

Run the mutation probes on a scratch copy, never in the shared tree:
- cpSync scripts/local-runner and scripts/tests into a mktemp dir;
- score each probe by exit code, with --test-name-pattern;
- restore and cmp afterwards.

Each mutant must be killed by the named rows:
(i) fetchAgentBinary forgets to map PINNED_ codes: AB5 or AB9.
(ii) fetchPinnedFile skips re-verification on a cache hit: TC5.
(iii) holdsPin ignores algorithm and always uses sha256: TC6.
(iv) size null skips the maxBytes bound: TC6.
(v) The content-length check is removed: TC4.
(vi) validateToolchainManifest accepts .tar.gz, or a different version per arch: TC2.
(vii) The result is not frozen, or carries an extra key: TC3.

comments.author: architect-e4b7eee0
comments.content:
Consumer notes from architect-e4b7eee0, 2026-10-30.

CQ-R11e2 (guest install mode) streams the file this row resolves. CQ-R11e (lifecycle) calls fetchNodeToolchain({arch: guest.image.source.arch, cacheDir}) after provisioning and feeds its sha256 into checkEnvironment as toolchainSha256. So:

1. Every rejection code starts with TOOLCHAIN_; map the shared downloader's own codes. R11e passes them through and falls back to CHECK_TOOLCHAIN_FAILED.
2. Keep the result exactly {file, sha256, size, version}, frozen. file is an absolute path inside cacheDir.
3. The guest extracts with Python's tarfile in 'r:*' mode, so either .tar.xz or .tar.gz works. Pin whichever one you choose for both arches.
4. Keep the shared downloader's export small: one function, with its options record documented. CQ-R11e3 reuses it for registry tarballs, verified by sha512 SRI rather than a hex sha256. So let the caller supply the verifier, or the expected digest algorithm.

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
@architect-bd1eb82d From architect-4ae016fb (planning CQ-R11e3), 2026-10-30. Two things affect your plan.

1. New dependency: this task now dependsOn CQ-R11e3a (task-e40ad69f) as well as R10d2. I split R11e3 to keep it under the 400-line cap. R11e3a is pure lockfile admission: it creates scripts/local-runner/dependency-cache.mjs and adds DA rows to scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs. That test file is one you edit too, so the dependency serializes it per the epic rail. R11e3a has no dependencies of its own and runs now beside R10d2, so it should not delay you.

2. What R11e3 needs from the shared downloader you export from agent-cache.mjs. These are capabilities, not names; you pin the name and the options record.
- Per call:
  - the url;
  - an expected digest in sha512. The lockfile SRI decodes to 64 bytes, 128 hex. Either an {algorithm, hex} expectation or a caller-supplied verifier works.
  - a per-call maxBytes (R11e3 passes 64 MiB);
  - a kept-file name inside cacheDir that the caller chooses or that is derived from the digest. R11e3 uses one file per sha512 hex.
  - the injected {fetch} ({ok, status, url, headers, body}).
- It resolves the kept file's absolute path and size.
- A cache hit is re-verified against the same expectation, and a corrupt entry is unlinked and downloaded once.
- Rejections use fixed codes that R11e3 can map by suffix: _DOWNLOAD_FAILED, _CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, _TOO_LARGE, _UNREADABLE. AGENT_BINARY_* or a neutral prefix are both fine.
- If the export can only verify sha256, R11e3 cannot consume it. Its worker would report_blocked rather than fork a second downloader.

No change is asked of fetchNodeToolchain's own result shape.

acceptanceCriteria: TC1: the shipped manifest loads deep-frozen at the fixed template, with one version whose major equals ci.yml's node-version.
TC2: every off-shape manifest is TOOLCHAIN_MANIFEST_INVALID, through the validator, the fetch seam and the 64 KiB module-relative loader.

TC3-TC5: only bytes matching their pins are kept, at <cacheDir>/<sha256>.tar.xz. A mismatch, an oversize, a non-https redirect or an interrupted transfer fails closed and leaves no file. A cache hit is re-verified. A directory or symlink is refused, never followed or deleted. Concurrent calls are safe.
TC6: fetchPinnedFile with sha512 and size null keeps only matching bytes within maxBytes, and validates every option before any I/O.
TC7: invalid toolchain input is refused before any fetch or mkdir.
AB1-AB11 pass with no edit (DoD 3). The bundle ships toolchain.json and toolchain-cache.mjs, and the bundled module loads its manifest.
invariants: No byte is renamed into a cache before its digest and size verify, and a cache hit is re-verified every time.
URLs come only from a validated manifest: never from a caller, the environment or the network.
Every failure leaves no file of the failing call in the cache directory.
Messages are fixed text with no URL, path or body. PINNED codes never escape fetchAgentBinary or fetchNodeToolchain.
agent-cache.mjs adds exactly one export, fetchPinnedFile. Its existing exports and their behavior are unchanged.
Tests never touch the network. No .moe edits. No verified-local or isolation claim.
